source_refs.note: Roman Urdu: practice short questions written from Unit 10 (PDF 182-204), not printed in the book; same questions and order as the English set. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Yeh Unit 10 (Trigonometric Identities) ke poore unit se practice short questions (mukhtasar sawal) hain, unit ke sections ki tarteeb mein, Board ke 2 number wale sawal ke andaz mein. Har sawal mukhtasar qadmon mein hal kiya gaya hai.

blocks.prompt:
1 Find the distance between the points \((-1, -2)\) and \((5, 6)\).
(Points \((-1, -2)\) aur \((5, 6)\) ke darmiyan faasla nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: For this we need the formula for the distance between two points in a plane.

blocks.prompt:
2 The distance between \((1, k)\) and \((4, 5)\) is \(5\). Find the possible values of \(k\).
(\((1, k)\) aur \((4, 5)\) ke darmiyan faasla \(5\) hai. \(k\) ki mumkin qeematein nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: The order of subtraction does not matter, because the differences are squared.

blocks.prompt:
3 Find the distance between \((2\cos\theta, 0)\) and \((0, 2\sin\theta)\).
(\((2\cos\theta, 0)\) aur \((0, 2\sin\theta)\) ke darmiyan faasla nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: The coordinates may be numbers or trigonometric expressions; the method is the same.

blocks.prompt:
4 Show that \(A(0, 0)\), \(B(3, 4)\) and \(C(6, 0)\) are the vertices of an isosceles triangle.
(Dikhayein ke \(A(0, 0)\), \(B(3, 4)\) aur \(C(6, 0)\) isosceles triangle (do barabar sides wali triangle) ke vertices hain.)
blocks.explanation: \(AB = 5\), \(BC = 5\), \(AC = 6\). Do sides barabar hain, is liye triangle isosceles hai.

book_ref.quote: Taking the root of each term separately

blocks.prompt:
5 Verify the fundamental law \(\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta\) for \(\alpha = 90^{\circ}\), \(\beta = 60^{\circ}\).
(Fundamental law ko \(\alpha = 90^{\circ}\), \(\beta = 60^{\circ}\) ke liye verify karein.)

book_ref.quote: which is called the Fundamental Law of Trigonometry.

blocks.prompt:
6 If \(\sin\alpha = \frac{8}{17}\), \(\cos\alpha = \frac{15}{17}\), \(\sin\beta = \frac{4}{5}\) and \(\cos\beta = \frac{3}{5}\), find \(\cos(\alpha - \beta)\).
(Agar \(\sin\alpha = \frac{8}{17}\), \(\cos\alpha = \frac{15}{17}\), \(\sin\beta = \frac{4}{5}\), \(\cos\beta = \frac{3}{5}\) hon to \(\cos(\alpha - \beta)\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Although we have proved this law for

blocks.prompt:
7 Write \(\cos 2\theta\cos\theta + \sin 2\theta\sin\theta\) as a single trigonometric ratio.
(\(\cos 2\theta\cos\theta + \sin 2\theta\sin\theta\) ko ek hi trigonometric ratio mein likhein.)

blocks.prompt:
8 Show by one example that \(\cos(\alpha - \beta) \ne \cos\alpha - \cos\beta\) in general.
(Ek misaal se dikhayein ke aam taur par \(\cos(\alpha - \beta) \ne \cos\alpha - \cos\beta\).)

book_ref.quote: Writing \(\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos\alpha - \cos\beta\)

blocks.prompt:
9 If \(\tan\alpha = 2\) and \(\tan\beta = 3\), find \(\tan(\alpha + \beta)\).
(Agar \(\tan\alpha = 2\) aur \(\tan\beta = 3\) ho to \(\tan(\alpha + \beta)\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Why divide by \(\cos\alpha\cos\beta\)? Because

blocks.prompt:
10 If \(\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5}\), \(\cos\alpha = \frac{4}{5}\), \(\sin\beta = \frac{5}{13}\) and \(\cos\beta = \frac{12}{13}\), find \(\sin(\alpha - \beta)\).
(Agar \(\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5}\), \(\cos\alpha = \frac{4}{5}\), \(\sin\beta = \frac{5}{13}\), \(\cos\beta = \frac{12}{13}\) hon to \(\sin(\alpha - \beta)\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: for sine the sign follows the bracket

blocks.prompt:
11 Prove that \(\dfrac{\sin(\alpha + \beta)}{\cos\alpha\cos\beta} = \tan\alpha + \tan\beta\).
(Sabit karein ke \(\dfrac{\sin(\alpha + \beta)}{\cos\alpha\cos\beta} = \tan\alpha + \tan\beta\).)
blocks.explanation: \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\) khol kar har term ko \(\cos\alpha\cos\beta\) se taqseem: \(\tan\alpha + \tan\beta\).

book_ref.quote: From the single law of 10.1.1 the book now deduces ten results

blocks.prompt:
12 Without tables, find \(\sin 165^{\circ}\) by writing \(165^{\circ} = 120^{\circ} + 45^{\circ}\).
(Tables ke baghair \(165^{\circ} = 120^{\circ} + 45^{\circ}\) likh kar \(\sin 165^{\circ}\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Quick use of (ix): \(\tan 75^{\circ} = \tan(45^{\circ} + 30^{\circ}) = \frac{1 + \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}{1 - \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}} = \frac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{\sqrt{3} - 1} = 2 + \sqrt{3}\)

blocks.prompt:
13 Prove that \(\cos(60^{\circ} + \theta) + \cos(60^{\circ} - \theta) = \cos\theta\).
(Sabit karein ke \(\cos(60^{\circ} + \theta) + \cos(60^{\circ} - \theta) = \cos\theta\).)
blocks.explanation: Dono khol kar sin wali terms cancel: \(2\cos 60^{\circ}\cos\theta = \cos\theta\).

book_ref.quote: changing the sign inside the bracket changes the sign in the middle

blocks.prompt:
14 Simplify \(\sin(30^{\circ} + \theta) - \cos(60^{\circ} + \theta)\).
(\(\sin(30^{\circ} + \theta) - \cos(60^{\circ} + \theta)\) ko simplify karein.)
blocks.explanation: Dono khol kar cos wali terms cancel: \(\sqrt{3}\sin\theta\).

book_ref.quote: Putting \(\beta = -\frac{\pi}{2}\) in it, we get

blocks.prompt:
15 Without tables, find \(\sin 510^{\circ}\).
(Tables ke baghair \(\sin 510^{\circ}\) nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(510^{\circ} = 5 \times 90^{\circ} + 60^{\circ}\): odd, sin cos ban jata hai; quadrant II mein sin musbat: \(\cos 60^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}\).

book_ref.quote: If \(n\) is even the ratio stays the same; if \(n\) is odd it changes to its co-ratio.

blocks.prompt:
16 Without tables, find \(\tan(-600^{\circ})\).
(Tables ke baghair \(\tan(-600^{\circ})\) nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(-\tan 600^{\circ}\); \(600^{\circ} = 6 \times 90^{\circ} + 60^{\circ}\) even, quadrant III mein tan musbat \(= \sqrt{3}\). Jawab \(-\sqrt{3}\).

book_ref.quote: For a negative angle, take the minus out first

blocks.prompt:
17 Without tables, find \(\sec 870^{\circ}\).
(Tables ke baghair \(\sec 870^{\circ}\) nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: \(870^{\circ} = 9 \times 90^{\circ} + 60^{\circ}\): odd, sec cosec banta hai; quadrant II mein sec manfi: \(-\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\).

book_ref.quote: The above results also apply to the reciprocals of sine, cosine and tangent.

blocks.prompt:
18 Express \(\cos 205^{\circ}\) as a trigonometric ratio of a positive angle less than \(45^{\circ}\).
(\(\cos 205^{\circ}\) ko \(45^{\circ}\) se chhote musbat angle ke ratio mein likhein.)

book_ref.quote: the ratios of a large angle can be found from those of an acute angle

blocks.prompt:
19 Express \(\tan 296^{\circ}\) as a trigonometric ratio of a positive angle less than \(45^{\circ}\).
(\(\tan 296^{\circ}\) ko \(45^{\circ}\) se chhote musbat angle ke ratio mein likhein.)
blocks.explanation: \(270^{\circ} + 26^{\circ}\): odd, tan cot banta hai; quadrant IV mein tan manfi: \(-\cot 26^{\circ}\).

book_ref.quote: the trigonometric ratios change into co-ratios and vice versa

blocks.prompt:
20 Prove that \(\sin(90^{\circ} + \theta)\cos(180^{\circ} - \theta) = -\cos^{2}\theta\).
(Sabit karein ke \(\sin(90^{\circ} + \theta)\cos(180^{\circ} - \theta) = -\cos^{2}\theta\).)

book_ref.quote: The sign of the result is decided by the quadrant in which the terminal arm of the angle lies.

blocks.prompt:
21 Prove that \(\tan(180^{\circ} - \theta) + \tan(360^{\circ} - \theta) + 2\tan\theta = 0\).
(Sabit karein ke \(\tan(180^{\circ} - \theta) + \tan(360^{\circ} - \theta) + 2\tan\theta = 0\).)

book_ref.quote: If \(\theta\) is added to or subtracted from an even multiple of

blocks.prompt:
22 Using \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \sin^{2}\alpha - \sin^{2}\beta\), find the value of \(\sin^{2}75^{\circ} - \sin^{2}15^{\circ}\).
(\(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\sin(\alpha - \beta) = \sin^{2}\alpha - \sin^{2}\beta\) se \(\sin^{2}75^{\circ} - \sin^{2}15^{\circ}\) ki qeemat nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Remember this result as a ready-made identity

blocks.prompt:
23 Show that \(\dfrac{1 + \tan 15^{\circ}}{1 - \tan 15^{\circ}} = \sqrt{3}\).
(Dikhayein ke \(\dfrac{1 + \tan 15^{\circ}}{1 - \tan 15^{\circ}} = \sqrt{3}\).)

book_ref.quote: appears often. In the same way

blocks.prompt:
24 If \(\cos\alpha = -\frac{5}{13}\) and the terminal side of \(\alpha\) is in quadrant II, find \(\sin\alpha\) and \(\tan\alpha\).
(Agar \(\cos\alpha = -\frac{5}{13}\) aur \(\alpha\) ki terminal side quadrant II mein ho to \(\sin\alpha\) aur \(\tan\alpha\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: choose each sign from the quadrant

blocks.prompt:
25 \(\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5}\) with \(\alpha\) in quadrant II and \(\cos\beta = -\frac{12}{13}\) with \(\beta\) in quadrant III. Find \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\).
(\(\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5}\) (\(\alpha\) quadrant II mein) aur \(\cos\beta = -\frac{12}{13}\) (\(\beta\) quadrant III mein). \(\cos(\alpha + \beta)\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: The square root gives two signs and the quadrant chooses one.

blocks.prompt:
26 With the data of the previous question, find \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\) and name the quadrant of \(\alpha + \beta\).
(Pichhle sawal ke data se \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\) nikalein aur \(\alpha + \beta\) ka quadrant batayein.)
blocks.explanation: \(\frac{-36 + 20}{65} = -\frac{16}{65}\). sin manfi, cos musbat: quadrant IV.

book_ref.quote: quadrant IV is the only quadrant where cosine is positive and sine is negative

blocks.prompt:
27 If \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) are the angles of a triangle, prove that \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\cos\gamma + \cos(\alpha + \beta)\sin\gamma = 0\).
(Agar \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) triangle ke angles hon to sabit karein ke \(\sin(\alpha + \beta)\cos\gamma + \cos(\alpha + \beta)\sin\gamma = 0\).)

book_ref.quote: In a triangle \(\alpha + \beta + \gamma = 180^{\circ}\)

blocks.prompt:
28 Express \(20\sin\theta + 21\cos\theta\) in the form \(r\sin(\theta + \phi)\), with \(\phi\) in quadrant I.
(\(20\sin\theta + 21\cos\theta\) ko \(r\sin(\theta + \phi)\) ki form mein likhein (\(\phi\) quadrant I mein).)

book_ref.quote: \(a\sin\theta + b\cos\theta = r\sin(\theta + \phi)\), \(r = \sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}\)

blocks.prompt:
29 Express \(\sqrt{3}\sin\theta + \cos\theta\) in the form \(r\sin(\theta + \phi)\) and give \(\phi\) in degrees.
(\(\sqrt{3}\sin\theta + \cos\theta\) ko \(r\sin(\theta + \phi)\) ki form mein likhein; \(\phi\) degrees mein dein.)

book_ref.quote: Because \(-1 \le \sin(\theta + \phi) \le 1\)

blocks.prompt:
30 If \(\cos\alpha = \frac{8}{17}\) and \(\alpha\) is acute, find \(\sin 2\alpha\) and \(\cos 2\alpha\).
(Agar \(\cos\alpha = \frac{8}{17}\) aur \(\alpha\) acute ho to \(\sin 2\alpha\) aur \(\cos 2\alpha\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Choose the one that contains what is given or what you need

blocks.prompt:
31 If \(\tan\alpha = 2\), find \(\tan 2\alpha\).
(Agar \(\tan\alpha = 2\) ho to \(\tan 2\alpha\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: The tangent formula works only when

blocks.prompt:
32 Prove that \(\dfrac{1 - \cos 2\theta}{1 + \cos 2\theta} = \tan^{2}\theta\).
(Sabit karein ke \(\dfrac{1 - \cos 2\theta}{1 + \cos 2\theta} = \tan^{2}\theta\).)

book_ref.quote: Rearranging the last two forms gives two very useful results

blocks.prompt:
33 Prove that \((\sin\theta + \cos\theta)^{2} = 1 + \sin 2\theta\).
(Sabit karein ke \((\sin\theta + \cos\theta)^{2} = 1 + \sin 2\theta\).)

book_ref.quote: we only have to put \(\beta = \alpha\) in the sum formulas

blocks.prompt:
34 Prove that \(\cos^{4}\theta - \sin^{4}\theta = \cos 2\theta\).
(Sabit karein ke \(\cos^{4}\theta - \sin^{4}\theta = \cos 2\theta\).)

book_ref.quote: has three equivalent forms

blocks.prompt:
35 If \(\sin\theta + \cos\theta = \frac{7}{5}\), find \(\sin 2\theta\).
(Agar \(\sin\theta + \cos\theta = \frac{7}{5}\) ho to \(\sin 2\theta\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Double angle identities come from the sum formulas with

blocks.prompt:
36 If \(\cos\alpha = \frac{1}{9}\) and \(\alpha\) is acute, find \(\sin\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\) and \(\cos\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\).
(Agar \(\cos\alpha = \frac{1}{9}\) aur \(\alpha\) acute ho to \(\sin\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\) aur \(\cos\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Half angle identities are the forms

blocks.prompt:
37 Using a half angle identity, find \(\cos 112.5^{\circ}\).
(Half angle identity se \(\cos 112.5^{\circ}\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Taking \(+\) here would give a wrong answer.

blocks.prompt:
38 If \(\cos\alpha = \frac{3}{5}\) and \(270^{\circ} < \alpha < 360^{\circ}\), find \(\tan\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\).
(Agar \(\cos\alpha = \frac{3}{5}\) aur \(270^{\circ} < \alpha < 360^{\circ}\) ho to \(\tan\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Choosing the sign from the quadrant of

blocks.prompt:
39 If \(\cos\alpha = -\frac{7}{9}\) and \(90^{\circ} < \alpha < 180^{\circ}\), find \(\sin\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\).
(Agar \(\cos\alpha = -\frac{7}{9}\) aur \(90^{\circ} < \alpha < 180^{\circ}\) ho to \(\sin\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: The sign is chosen from the quadrant of

blocks.prompt:
40 Using a half angle identity, show that \(\tan 22.5^{\circ} = \sqrt{2} - 1\).
(Half angle identity se dikhayein ke \(\tan 22.5^{\circ} = \sqrt{2} - 1\).)

book_ref.quote: These carry the correct sign automatically.

blocks.prompt:
41 Using \(\sin 3\alpha = 3\sin\alpha - 4\sin^{3}\alpha\), find \(\sin 3\alpha\) when \(\sin\alpha = \frac{1}{2}\), and check with \(\alpha = 30^{\circ}\).
(\(\sin 3\alpha = 3\sin\alpha - 4\sin^{3}\alpha\) se \(\sin\alpha = \frac{1}{2}\) par \(\sin 3\alpha\) nikalein aur \(\alpha = 30^{\circ}\) se check karein.)

book_ref.quote: We want the answer in \(\sin\alpha\) only

blocks.prompt:
42 Using \(\cos 3\alpha = 4\cos^{3}\alpha - 3\cos\alpha\), find \(\cos 3\alpha\) when \(\cos\alpha = \frac{1}{2}\), and check with \(\alpha = 60^{\circ}\).
(\(\cos 3\alpha = 4\cos^{3}\alpha - 3\cos\alpha\) se \(\cos\alpha = \frac{1}{2}\) par \(\cos 3\alpha\) nikalein aur \(\alpha = 60^{\circ}\) se check karein.)

book_ref.quote: Here we want the answer in \(\cos\alpha\) only

blocks.prompt:
43 If \(\tan\alpha = \frac{1}{3}\), find \(\tan 3\alpha\).
(Agar \(\tan\alpha = \frac{1}{3}\) ho to \(\tan 3\alpha\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Multiply the numerator and the denominator of the big fraction by

blocks.prompt:
44 Show that \(\sin^{3}\theta = \dfrac{3\sin\theta - \sin 3\theta}{4}\).
(Dikhayein ke \(\sin^{3}\theta = \dfrac{3\sin\theta - \sin 3\theta}{4}\).)

book_ref.quote: Every triple angle proof starts with

blocks.prompt:
45 If \(\tan\theta = \frac{1}{2}\), find \(\sin 2\theta\) and \(\cos 2\theta\) using only \(\tan\theta\).
(Agar \(\tan\theta = \frac{1}{2}\) ho to sirf \(\tan\theta\) se \(\sin 2\theta\) aur \(\cos 2\theta\) nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: They hold whenever \(\cos\theta \ne 0\).

blocks.text: 10.7 Express the Product (of sines and cosines) as Sums or Differences (of sines and cosines)

blocks.prompt:
46 Express \(2\sin 4\theta\cos 2\theta\) as a sum.
(\(2\sin 4\theta\cos 2\theta\) ko sum ki shakal mein likhein.)

book_ref.quote: Write the larger angle as

blocks.prompt:
47 Find the value of \(2\cos 75^{\circ}\sin 15^{\circ}\) without tables.
(Tables ke baghair \(2\cos 75^{\circ}\sin 15^{\circ}\) ki qeemat nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: cosine first): use the second line

blocks.prompt:
48 Find the value of \(2\sin 52.5^{\circ}\sin 7.5^{\circ}\) without tables.
(Tables ke baghair \(2\sin 52.5^{\circ}\sin 7.5^{\circ}\) ki qeemat nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: and do not forget its minus sign

blocks.prompt:
49 Express \(\sin 7\theta + \sin 3\theta\) as a product.
(\(\sin 7\theta + \sin 3\theta\) ko product mein likhein.)

book_ref.quote: In words: half the sum and half the difference of the two angles.

blocks.prompt:
50 Find the value of \(\cos 75^{\circ} - \cos 15^{\circ}\) without tables.
(Tables ke baghair \(\cos 75^{\circ} - \cos 15^{\circ}\) ki qeemat nikalein.)

book_ref.quote: Only the last one has a minus sign

blocks.prompt:
51 Prove that \(\sin 70^{\circ} - \sin 10^{\circ} = \cos 40^{\circ}\).
(Sabit karein ke \(\sin 70^{\circ} - \sin 10^{\circ} = \cos 40^{\circ}\).)

book_ref.quote: Sum to product: half sum and half difference
